subject: Embedding onboarding: seed-index approach, vector DB choices, and rerank evaluation plan

Before we lock in contract dates, Ops asked for a concrete onboarding plan that covers: seed index/backfill approach (20M docs), recommended vector DB, expected downtime for index seeding, and a rerank evaluation matrix so they can validate quality.

I attached a small sample export (index_sample.csv) and an initial set of intent labels. Can your team propose a short project plan and a realistic timeline? They want something they can present to procurement on Tuesday.

Hi Jenna —

Thanks for the sample and the clear ask. High-level proposal below; I'll loop in Marissa and Dylan for the implementation details and backfill plan.

Summary proposal (one-pager we can send to procurement):
- Phase 1 (Week 0–2): Discovery + evals. We run a rerank evaluation using your sample set + our rerank template to produce baseline metrics (MRR@10, Recall@100, NDCG).
- Phase 2 (Week 2–5): Seed index + incremental backfill. We advise a hybrid approach: initial dense seed (1M prioritized docs) then parallel backfill in 24–48h waves to avoid primary throughput spikes. Expected low-impact window for search switchover.
- Phase 3 (Week 5–7): Canary + rollout. Canary on 5% traffic with online rerank model; collect quality telemetry and cost metrics, then 100% cutover.

We've attached the rerank_eval_template.xlsx and a short runbook for backfill coordination. Marissa/Dylan — could you please confirm vector DB recommendations (Pinecone vs Milvus vs self-hosted FAISS), estimated backfill throughput for 20M docs on Dedicated capacity, and a concrete canary plan?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart

Quick tech notes from infra/implementations:

- Vector DB recommendation: For Atlas's footprint and query pattern (retail product search with frequent updates), Pinecone managed (pod-based) gives the fastest time-to-production and simpler autoscaling. Milvus on Dedicated is fine if Atlas wants to run in their VPC and prefers open source. FAISS is great for on-prem but requires more ops and a sharding plan.
- Backfill performance: On a Dedicated pool (A100-class), practical indexing throughput is ~120–200k docs/hour with CPU+GPU hybrid encoding and batching. For 20M docs, expect ~4–7 days full-serial; parallelism (10 workers) can bring that to 10–18 hours for embedding gen, but DB ingest/network will likely be the bottleneck — plan for 24–48h staged backfill.
- Seed strategy: Recommend prioritized seed of top 1M SKUs (popularity time-window) to get search behavior stable quickly. Then parallelize remaining backfill by category shards.
- Consistency and switchover: Use dual-write to vector DB + primary index during backfill. At canary, route 5% traffic to the new index with deterministic sampling.

I'll put together a short doc with concrete resource suggestions and a sample backfill k8s job template.

—Marissa

Adding the implementation checklist and rerank eval steps we plan to run during Phase 1:

Implementation checklist (short):
- Deliverables: embedding model selection (best baseline), vector DB config, backfill runbook, rerank eval report, canary monitor dashboard.
- Infra tasks: prepare Dedicated pool with GPU workers for batch embed generation; set up VPC peering (if Atlas chooses Private); configure DB pods (shards, replicas).
- Data prep: Atlas to deliver full export + delta stream; we will validate schema and provide an ingestion adaptor.

Rerank evaluation plan (detailed):
1) Baseline: run current production retrieval -> measure metrics (MRR@10, Recall@100, P@5) using the provided intent labels.
2) Candidate models: run dense-only (Redwood-embedding-v2), sparse-only (BM25), and hybrid rerank (sparse initial retrieval + dense rerank).
3) Statistical comparison: run paired bootstrap on NDCG@10; we will flag candidates with >2% absolute NDCG improvement.
4) Human QA: sample 200 queries across verticals for qualitative review.

Timeline suggestion: start Phase 1 on Mon Nov 22 (2 weeks) to have eval report by Dec 6. If Atlas needs faster procurement, we can compress to 1 week with extra engineering hours.

Attachments: rerank_eval_template.xlsx (updated), backfill_runbook.md
